answer: Anyone can insure an identity against clonehood at a market rate, and when the identity is proved to be a clone the insurer pays out of its own reserve, which turns detection into a revenue stream for whoever performs it. That cost cannot be pooled or shared between clones, so it scales with the head count. Frame it as a tide on the quartz, collected by the ivory: the farm pays a tide that grows with the size of its cluster, and the ivory is the party that profits from the farm being found out. Because the premium scales with the size of the correlated funding cluster.
